overview.heading: To the Foot of Mount Everest
overview.subheading: Through the spiritual heartland of the Sherpa people
overview.content:
The Everest Base Camp trek stands as one of the world's quintessential mountain journeys — a pilgrimage through landscapes so dramatic and a culture so deeply rooted in mountain tradition that each step carries the weight of adventure history. Beginning with an exhilarating scenic mountain flight into Lukla's legendary Tenzing-Hillary Airport, you step directly into high Himalayan terrain where suspension bridges draped with prayer flags span turquoise glacial rivers tumbling from peaks above 8,000 metres.

Over two carefully paced weeks, you will acclimatise in the bustling Sherpa trading capital of Namche Bazaar, perched amphitheatre-like above the confluence of the Bhote Kosi and Dudh Koshi rivers. From here, the trail ascends through silver birch forests to the spiritual sanctuary of Tengboche Monastery — backdropped by the soaring spike of Ama Dablam — before continuing through the high-altitude villages of Dingboche and Lobuche toward the lunar moraine landscape of Gorak Shep.

Standing at Everest Base Camp (5,364m) before the formidable churning walls of the Khumbu Icefall, then watching the Himalayan dawn ignite the summit pyramid of Everest from the rocky crest of Kala Patthar (5,550m) are defining moments that transform every trekker who completes them. Throughout the journey, a dedicated team of government-licensed guides and experienced Sherpa porters ensure your safety, comfort, and access to authentic mountain culture at every stage.
overview.highlight: A demanding yet deeply rewarding Himalayan journey defined by altitude, shifting mountain landscapes, rich Sherpa cultural heritage, and unforgettable views beneath the world's highest summits — including Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, and Cho Oyu.
highlights: Stand at Everest Base Camp (5,364m) directly before the iconic Khumbu Icefall
Dawn climb of Kala Patthar (5,550m) for panoramic sunrise views of Mount Everest
Two acclimatisation nights in Namche Bazaar with guided cultural hikes
Visit the revered Tengboche Monastery with direct views of Ama Dablam
Cross legendary Hillary and Tenzing suspension bridges adorned with prayer flags
Hike above the clouds through Sagarmatha National Park's pristine alpine forests
Full private guide, Sherpa porter, and medical safety kit support throughout

itinerary_section.heading: 15 Days Through the Khumbu Valley
itinerary_section.subtext: Open each day to inspect the planned trail route, elevation profile, meals, accommodation, and estimated walking times. All days include dedicated guide and porter support.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Kathmandu & Boutique Hotel Transfer
itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! Upon clearing customs at Tribhuvan International Airport, an expedition representative will greet you and escort you by private vehicle to your boutique heritage hotel in central Kathmandu. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon to recover from your journey before a comprehensive pre-trek briefing covering equipment checks, permit documentation, and daily logistics. The evening concludes with a traditional Nepali welcome dinner.
itinerary.pills: Meals: Welcome Dinner · Boutique Heritage Hotel · Kathmandu

itinerary.title: Scenic Mountain Flight to Lukla & Trek to Phakding
itinerary.description: An early morning departure for the iconic 35-minute scenic mountain flight to Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla — one of the world's most dramatically situated runways, perched on a cliff edge at 2,840m. Meet your Sherpa trekking crew, distribute loads to porters, and begin the gentle downward trail along the Dudh Koshi riverbank through fragrant pine and rhododendron woodland to the river village of Phakding. Cross two suspension bridges adorned with colourful prayer flags as yak caravans pass by.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Teahouse Lodge · Approx. 3–4 hrs

itinerary.title: Ascend to the Sherpa Capital of Namche Bazaar
itinerary.description: Today's trail crosses the spectacular Hillary Suspension Bridge — one of the highest suspension bridges in Nepal — before entering Sagarmatha National Park at Jorsale checkpoint. A sustained two-hour zig-zag ascent through mixed forest brings you to the amphitheatre of Namche Bazaar, the vibrant Sherpa capital and commercial hub of the Khumbu region. On a clear day, your first thrilling glimpse of Mount Everest appears framed through the trees just before you crest the ridge into town.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation Day: Everest View Hotel Hike & Sherpa Museum
itinerary.description: A critical and rewarding acclimatisation rest day. Following the 'climb high, sleep low' principle, you will hike up to the famous Everest View Hotel (3,880m) for sweeping 180-degree panoramas of Ama Dablam, Thamserku, Kantega, and — on a clear morning — the distinctive summit pyramid of Mount Everest rising above the Lhotse–Nuptse ridge. In the afternoon, explore the informative Sherpa Culture Museum in Namche and browse the weekend market.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Acclimatisation Hike 3–4 hrs

itinerary.title: Trail to Tengboche Monastery with Ama Dablam Views
itinerary.description: Leaving Namche, a contour path weaves above the Imja Khola before descending steeply to the river crossing at Phunki Tenga (3,250m) — a welcome lunch stop beneath towering fir trees. A sustained two-hour climb through silver birch and conifer forest leads to the dramatic ridge-top sanctuary of Tengboche Monastery, the largest and most sacred monastery in the Khumbu. The setting is extraordinary: the monastery stands directly before the soaring triangular peak of Ama Dablam (6,812m), with Everest, Lhotse, and Nuptse visible behind.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Trek Through Pangboche to High-Altitude Dingboche
itinerary.description: Descend from Tengboche through open meadows and juniper scrub into the lower Khumbu, visiting the ancient Pangboche Monastery — the oldest in the region — before crossing the Imja Khola and ascending sharply into the broad hanging valley of Dingboche. This elevated settlement (4,410m) marks your transition into the true high Himalayan zone: the vegetation is sparse, yak herding dominates, and the peaks crowd the horizon in every direction. Evenings at this altitude are cold; retire early and drink plenty of fluids.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation Day: Nangkartshang Peak Hike
itinerary.description: A second essential acclimatisation day. An early morning hike up the flank of Nangkartshang Peak (5,083m) rewards with exceptional views of Island Peak (Imja Tse), Makalu, Baruntse, and the full Lhotse–Nuptse wall. This altitude gain significantly prepares your body for the high camps ahead. Return to Dingboche for a hearty lunch, afternoon rest, and pre-dinner briefing on Lobuche and the approach to Base Camp.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Hike 4–5 hrs

itinerary.title: Trek to Lobuche Past Memorial Chortens
itinerary.description: The trail climbs steeply out of Dingboche, crossing the lateral moraine of the Khumbu Glacier and emerging onto the bleak but starkly beautiful Khumbu plateau. Before reaching Lobuche, you pass the sobering Chukpilhara Memorial — rows of white chortens commemorating climbers and Sherpas lost on Everest. At 4,940m, the air is noticeably thinner; headaches are common and appetite often reduces. Stay well-hydrated, maintain a slow pace, and inform your guide of any altitude symptoms.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Teahouse · Approx. 4–5 hrs

itinerary.stage: Lobuche (4,940m) → Gorak Shep (5,140m) → Everest Base Camp (5,364m)
itinerary.title: The Day You've Trained For: Everest Base Camp!
itinerary.description: The culmination of your Himalayan journey. The trail from Lobuche follows the eastern flank of the Khumbu Glacier across rocky lateral moraine terrain to the seasonal outpost of Gorak Shep (5,140m) — the last teahouse before Base Camp — where packs are deposited and a light lunch is taken. The final two-hour route to Base Camp (5,364m) traverses the undulating surface of the glacier itself, a surreal landscape of blue ice towers, meltwater streams, and coloured expedition tents. Standing beneath the thundering seracs of the Khumbu Icefall, with the West Shoulder of Everest directly above, is an experience of pure, unequalled Himalayan majesty.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Gorak Shep Teahouse · Approx. 7–8 hrs total

itinerary.title: Dawn Summit of Kala Patthar & Descent to Pheriche
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn alarm at 04:30. By headtorch, ascend the steep scree and rocky ridge of Kala Patthar (5,550m) as the Himalayan sky transforms from deep purple to blazing amber gold. The summit vantage point delivers one of the greatest panoramas on Earth: the triangular summit of Mount Everest rising impossibly above the South Col, flanked by Lhotse, Nuptse, Changtse, Pumori, and the Rongbuk Glacier valley stretching north toward Tibet. After photographs, descend to Gorak Shep for a late breakfast before a long, descending trail to the lower village of Pheriche.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Village Teahouse · Approx. 8–9 hrs total

itinerary.title: Long Descent Back to Namche Bazaar
itinerary.description: The descent from Pheriche to Namche is a long but joyful day as the air thickens and vegetation returns. Retrace familiar trails through Pangboche and Tengboche — now seen from a fresh perspective with Base Camp already behind you. A sustained descent through birch forest and across the Phunki Tenga river bridges leads back into the welcoming warmth of Namche Bazaar. Celebrate with a sunset beer and dinner at a favourite Namche restaurant, reflecting on the remarkable week just completed.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 7–8 hrs

itinerary.title: Final Trail Day: Namche to Lukla
itinerary.description: A bittersweet final trekking day retracing the now-familiar trail from Namche through Monjo, past the park checkpoint, and back along the Dudh Koshi riverbank to Phakding — this time moving efficiently with the trail already etched in memory. A sustained ascent from Phakding through the forest canopy returns you to Lukla's main street, where the trekking crew rests and groups gather for farewell moments. A traditional crew-celebration dinner with your guide, Sherpas, and porters rounds out an extraordinary journey.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Lukla Lodge · Approx. 6–7 hrs

itinerary.title: Scenic Mountain Flight Back to Kathmandu
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, transfer to Lukla Airport for the return scenic mountain flight to Kathmandu — a final aerial salute to the peaks that hosted your extraordinary journey. Transfer to your hotel for hot showers, fresh city food, and a well-earned afternoon of leisure. The evening is free for souvenir shopping in Thamel's vibrant bazaars or a quiet dinner in Kathmandu's increasingly sophisticated restaurant scene.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B · Boutique City Hotel · Mountain Flight

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu: Heritage & Culture
itinerary.description: A full free day in Kathmandu to explore at leisure or join an optional guided heritage tour. Recommended highlights include a rickshaw tour through the medieval lanes of Bhaktapur Durbar Square (UNESCO), meditation at the Buddhist stupa of Boudhanath, sunset views from the hilltop temple of Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), and lunch at the garden terrace of the Hyatt Regency overlooking the Bagmati valley. A complimentary post-trek health consultation is also available through our expedition medical partner.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B · Boutique City Hotel · Free Day / Optional Tours

itinerary.title: Farewell & International Departure
itinerary.description: Your final morning in Nepal. Enjoy a last Himalayan breakfast before a private vehicle transfers you to Tribhuvan International Airport in ample time for your onward international flight. Our expedition team will coordinate baggage, documentation, and any last-minute logistics to ensure a smooth and memorable departure. Safe travels — and we hope to see you again soon on the trails.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B · Airport Transfer · Departure Day

inex.heading: Inclusions & Exclusions
inex.subtext: Everything included in your bespoke Himalayan journey, with no hidden surprises. Our all-inclusive pricing is designed so you can focus entirely on the trail.

inclusions.title: All private airport and domestic transfers
inclusions.desc: Private chauffeur-driven transfers in air-conditioned vehicles between Kathmandu Tribhuvan International Airport, hotels, and all domestic transfer points throughout the journey.

inclusions.title: Return scenic mountain flights (Kathmandu–Lukla–Kathmandu)
inclusions.desc: Return Twin Otter or Dornier scenic mountain flights on the world-famous Kathmandu–Lukla route, including all airport departure taxes and 15kg total baggage allowance per traveller.

inclusions.title: All government permits, TIMS card & National Park entry fees
inclusions.desc: Sagarmatha National Park entry clearances, TIMS (Trekkers' Information Management System) card, and Khumbu Pasang Lhamu rural municipality permits — all arranged and paid in advance by our team.

inclusions.title: Licensed English-speaking senior mountain guide
inclusions.desc: Government-licensed senior high-altitude trekking guide certified in wilderness first aid and altitude management, with pulse oximeter for twice-daily blood oxygen monitoring of all trekkers.

inclusions.title: Experienced Sherpa porters (1 porter per 2 trekkers, 12kg limit)
inclusions.desc: Dedicated Sherpa porters assigned on a 1:2 ratio with a strict maximum of 12kg of client luggage per porter, per Sherpa welfare industry standards. Porter wages, insurance, and equipment are fully covered.

inclusions.title: Boutique hotel stays in Kathmandu (2 nights each way)
inclusions.desc: 4/5-star boutique heritage hotel accommodation in central Kathmandu on a twin-share basis with daily breakfast included. Upgrades to private suites available on request.

inclusions.title: Comfortable mountain teahouse lodges throughout the trek
inclusions.desc: Pre-selected, highest-standard teahouse accommodation with private or twin rooms along the Everest trail, with three meals daily cooked fresh to order from lodge menus.

exclusions.title: International flights to and from Kathmandu
exclusions.desc: Long-haul international airfares to and from Tribhuvan International Airport (Kathmandu), and any associated international baggage overages, are not included in the land price.

exclusions.title: Nepal tourist visa fees
exclusions.desc: Nepal tourist visas are payable on arrival at Kathmandu International Airport in cash USD. Fees: USD 30 (15 days), USD 50 (30 days), USD 125 (90 days). Bring passport-size photos and exact USD cash.

exclusions.title: High-altitude emergency travel & medical evacuation insurance
exclusions.desc: Mandatory comprehensive travel insurance explicitly covering helicopter emergency evacuation to 6,000m, medical emergencies, trip cancellation, and personal liability. This is a non-negotiable safety requirement.

exclusions.title: Personal trekking equipment & technical apparel
exclusions.desc: Personal four-season sleeping bag (−10°C comfort rating), down jacket, technical hiking boots, trekking poles, headlamp, and all personal clothing. Equipment hire available in Kathmandu and Namche Bazaar.

exclusions.title: Bottled beverages, hot showers, device charging & Wi-Fi
exclusions.desc: Bottled mineral water, hot beverages beyond included meals, alcoholic beverages, hot showers, solar device charging fees, and Wi-Fi access at teahouses (typically NPR 200–500 per device per day).

exclusions.title: Gratuities for expedition crew
exclusions.desc: Tipping of guiding and porter crew at the conclusion of the trek is customary and deeply appreciated. Recommended guidelines: Lead guide USD 10–15/day, Porters USD 5–8/day per trekker.

essential.heading: Essential Information for Your Everest Journey
essential.intro: Careful preparation and sound health awareness ensure a safe, successful, and deeply rewarding Himalayan journey. Our expedition team has compiled these evidence-based recommendations for every Everest Base Camp trekker.
essential.card_desc: Includes detailed packing checklist, altitude acclimatisation schedule, Nepal visa guidelines, medical preparation advice, and seasonal weather data.

faqs.question: What is the best season to undertake the Everest Base Camp trek?
faqs.answer:
The two premier trekking seasons are Autumn (mid-September to late November) and Spring (early March to late May). Autumn offers crisp, clear skies after the monsoon, vivid mountain visibility, and moderate temperatures. Spring brings longer days, blooming rhododendron valleys, and the visual drama of expedition teams on the mountain. Both seasons offer outstanding conditions; spring is slightly warmer at lower elevations.

  • Autumn: September–November — Best overall visibility
  • Spring: March–May — Warmer, flowers in bloom
  • Winter: December–February — Possible but very cold; fewer trekkers
  • Monsoon: June–August — Not recommended; heavy rain and leeches

faqs.question: How fit do I need to be, and how is altitude sickness managed?
faqs.answer:
You do not need to be an extreme athlete, but a solid foundation of cardiovascular aerobic fitness is essential. Our recommended pre-trek training includes 8–12 weeks of regular hiking on hilly terrain with a loaded pack, plus swimming or cycling for cardio base. Our itineraries incorporate two built-in acclimatisation rest days at Namche Bazaar (3,440m) and Dingboche (4,410m), following the internationally recognised 'climb high, sleep low' principle.

Altitude sickness (Acute Mountain Sickness / AMS) is managed through: strict ascent rate limits (no more than 300–500m net gain per day above 3,000m), twice-daily pulse oximeter blood oxygen readings by your lead Sherpa guide, immediate descent protocols if symptoms worsen, and ready access to supplemental oxygen and emergency evacuation services.

faqs.question: What type of accommodation and food can I expect on the trail?
faqs.answer:
In Kathmandu, you stay at 4/5-star boutique heritage hotels with en-suite bathrooms, international breakfast buffets, and city-centre locations. On the trekking route, accommodation is in the best available mountain teahouse lodges — typically twin-share rooms with comfortable beds, blankets, and attached bathroom facilities at lower elevations, with basic shared bathrooms at higher altitudes (Lobuche, Gorak Shep).

Trail food is hearty and surprisingly varied: dal bhat (rice and lentil), pasta, pizza, soups, porridge, pancakes, fried rice, noodles, and fresh baked goods are all available from teahouse menus. All dietary requirements — vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free — are easily accommodated with advance notice.

reviews.name: Sarah & David Jenkins
reviews.quote: Standing beneath Everest was breathtaking, but what truly elevated our entire expedition was the unmatched warmth, expertise, and professionalism of our Sherpa team. Every detail was perfectly planned. We are already dreaming of the Annapurna Circuit next year.

reviews.name: Marcus Vance
reviews.quote: The two built-in acclimatisation days made an enormous difference — I felt genuinely strong at Base Camp and Kala Patthar. The sunrise from Kala Patthar was the most stunning thing I have ever witnessed. Our guide Dawa was exceptional in every way.

reviews.name: Priya Mehta

overview.heading: Across the Great Himalayan Divide
overview.subheading: From lush subtropical valleys to the rain shadow of Mustang
overview.content:
The Annapurna Circuit is widely celebrated as one of the world's most diverse long-distance treks. Over 16 unforgettable days, you journey from terraced subtropical rice paddies and tumbling waterfalls through dense rhododendron and oak forests, rising steadily into the arid, windswept high-altitude plateau of Manang reminiscent of the Tibetan highlands.

Acclimatising in the medieval village of Manang beneath the imposing north face of Annapurna II, III, and Gangapurna prepares you for the trek's ultimate challenge: the pre-dawn crossing of Thorong La Pass at 5,416 metres. Descending into the sacred pilgrimage valley of Muktinath and onward through the dramatic Kali Gandaki gorge — the deepest gorge on Earth — completes an epic journey spanning cultures, religions, and ecosystems.
overview.highlight: An extraordinary journey crossing from lush green valleys into the arid Tibetan-influenced realm of Mustang, crowned by the high-altitude achievement of the 5,416m Thorong La Pass.

Relax in the tranquil lakeside paradise of Pokhara with views of Machapuchare

itinerary_section.heading: 16 Days Encircling the Annapurna Massif
itinerary_section.subtext: Explore each day's trail details, elevation profiles, overnight stops, and walking times. Fully supported with private guides and porters.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Kathmandu & Expedition Briefing
itinerary.description: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport and private transfer to your boutique heritage hotel. Welcome drink, comprehensive pre-trek briefing, gear inspection, and traditional Nepali welcome dinner.
itinerary.pills: Meals: Welcome Dinner · Boutique Hotel

itinerary.title: Scenic Overland Drive into the Marshyangdi Valley
itinerary.description: Scenic morning drive from Kathmandu along the Prithvi Highway, following the Trishuli and Marshyangdi rivers past Besisahar to Dharapani. Transition from lush foothills to alpine landscapes.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Teahouse · Approx. 7–8 hrs drive

itinerary.title: Trek Through Pine Forests to District Capital Chame
itinerary.description: The trail weaves through dense pine and oak forests, crossing suspension bridges over the thundering Marshyangdi River with dramatic views of Lamjung Himal and Annapurna II ahead.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Walk Beneath the Dramatic Paungda Danda Rock Face
itinerary.description: Enter the upper valley where the landscape becomes markedly drier. Gaze upon the smooth curved granite wall of Paungda Danda (Swargadwari) rising 1,500m above the river before reaching Pisang.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Teahouse · Approx. 5 hrs

itinerary.title: High Route via Ghyaru & Ngawal with Panoramic Views
itinerary.description: Follow the breathtaking upper route via Ghyaru and Ngawal, offering commanding vistas of Annapurna II, III, IV, Gangapurna, and Tilicho Peak before descending to the ancient trading village of Manang.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 6–7 hrs

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation Day: Gangapurna Lake & Chongkor Viewpoint
itinerary.description: Rest and acclimatise in Manang. Take an excursion to turquoise Gangapurna Lake and the Chongkor viewpoint for panoramic mountain photography. Visit the Himalayan Rescue Association clinic for an altitude lecture.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · 3–4 hrs hike

itinerary.title: Ascend Above the Treeline into Alpine Scrub
itinerary.description: Leave the valley floor and climb steadily out of the Marshyangdi Valley, passing juniper shrubs and grazing blue sheep to reach the high alpine pasture settlement of Yak Kharka.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Alpine Teahouse · Approx. 4 hrs

itinerary.title: Trek to High Camp / Thorong Phedi
itinerary.description: A short but demanding climb across a dramatic scree slope to the base of the pass at Thorong Phedi. Rest early in preparation for the pre-dawn summit departure tomorrow morning.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · High Teahouse · Approx. 3–4 hrs

itinerary.stage: Thorong Phedi (4,540m) → Thorong La Pass (5,416m) → Muktinath (3,800m)
itinerary.title: Conquer Thorong La Pass & Descend to Sacred Muktinath
itinerary.description: A pre-dawn 04:00 start by headlamp. Ascend the steep switchbacks to the prayer-flag strewn crest of Thorong La Pass (5,416m) under sunrise. Celebrate this pinnacle achievement before a long 1,600m descent into sacred Muktinath.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Village Lodge · 8–9 hrs total

itinerary.title: Trek Through the Kali Gandaki Valley to Apple Capital Marpha
itinerary.description: Visit Muktinath's sacred 108 water spouts and perpetual flame before trekking down through the dramatic, wind-sculpted Kali Gandaki valley past Jomsom to the charming whitewashed village of Marpha, famed for its apple orchards and cider.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Heritage Teahouse · Approx. 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Overland Drive to Natural Hot Springs at Tatopani
itinerary.description: Scenic transfer through the deepest section of the Kali Gandaki Gorge between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna to the riverside oasis of Tatopani. Relax your muscles in the therapeutic natural hot spring pools.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Garden Lodge · Approx. 4 hrs drive

itinerary.title: Climb Through Rhododendron Forests to Ghorepani
itinerary.description: A sustained climb ascending from subtropical orchards through lush rhododendron and magnolia forests to the picturesque ridge settlement of Ghorepani beneath the gaze of Dhaulagiri.
itinerary.pills: Meals: B, L, D · Mountain Lodge · Approx. 6–7 hrs

itinerary.title: Dawn Sunrise at Poon Hill & Transfer to Lakeside Pokhara
itinerary.description: Pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) for an iconic sunrise panorama spanning Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Manaslu. Descend to Nayapul and drive to your luxury lakeside hotel in Pokhara.

faqs.question: How challenging is the Thorong La Pass crossing?
faqs.answer: Thorong La (5,416m) is a strenuous high-altitude pass. The ascent from Thorong Phedi takes 4–5 hours on steep terrain in sub-zero pre-dawn temperatures, followed by a 1,600m descent to Muktinath. Proper acclimatisation at Manang is essential for a safe, successful crossing.

faqs.question: What kind of clothing is required for the temperature variation?
faqs.answer: Temperatures vary widely: from +25°C in the subtropical valleys to −15°C at Thorong La. A four-season layering system is essential, including thermal base layers, fleece mid-layers, windproof/waterproof outer shells, and a heavy down jacket.
